entry.name: waveform~
entry.description: Use the waveform~ object to view or edit the contents of a buffer~.

attributes.name: allowdrag
attributes.description: Toggles drag & drop functionality.

attributes.name: annotation
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: attr_bpm
attributes.description: Specifies beats per minute as the time reference unit relative to a tempo and number of beats per bar, both of which you can set with themessage.can also calculate a tempo that fits your current selection, via themessage.

attributes.name: background
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: beats
attributes.description: Toggles the display of time in beat units if theobject is set to display time in bpm units (set using theattribute). The default is 0 (off).

attributes.name: bgcolor
attributes.description: Sets the background color in RGBA format used to paint the entire object rectangle before the rest of the display components are drawn on top.

attributes.name: buffername
attributes.description: Sets the name of theobject.

attributes.name: chanoffset
attributes.description: Specifies a given channel in a multi-channel audio file to be displayed. Channel numbering starts at 1, and values must be in the range 1-4.

attributes.name: clipdraw
attributes.description: When set to 1, will cause values being edited in draw mode to be clipped to the range of the display (as determined by themessage).disables clipping, allowing values to be scaled freely beyond the range of the window. The default is 0, no clipping.

attributes.description: Specifies that the selection start and end points should snap to the vertical grid lines, as set by themessage. Since the spacing of the grid lines is affected by the current time measurement unit, and by the offset value (if an offset has been specified), snap to grid will be affected by these parameters as well.

attributes.name: gridcolor
attributes.description: Sets the gridcolor in RGBA format. Theattribute is mapped to thestyle color.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.description: Toggles the display of the numerical labels of time measurement across the top of the display. Any non-zero int causes the labels to be drawn. An argument of, or no argument, disables them.

attributes.digest: Ruler area click and drag toggle
attributes.description: Toggles clicking and dragging in the ruler area of thedisplay. The default is enabled.

attributes.name: offset
attributes.digest: Label and time measurement marking shift
attributes.description: Causes all labels and time measurement markings to be shifted by a specified number of milliseconds. Snap behavior is shifted as well.can be removed by sending the message, or themessage with no argument.

attributes.description: Determines when selection start and end values are sent in response to mouse activity. Only the selection start and end (outlets 3 and 4) are affected. attributes.name: selectalpha
attributes.description: This attribute is used to import older patches that containobjects. Previously, the selection rectangle is painted using two legacy messages (rgb2 and rgb7) and a "blend" transfer mode. Max uses the alpha channel to set the selection color, and will automatically apply this attribute to older version patches containing this object. rectangle.

attributes.name: selectioncolor
attributes.description: Sets the selection rectangle color which identifies the selection range in RGBA format.

attributes.name: setmode
attributes.description: Determines how theobject responds to mouse activity.

choices.label: Causesto enter a "display only" mode, in which clicking and dragging have no effect. For convenience, and to add custom interface behavior, mouse activity is still sent according to the mouseoutput mode. Amessage with no argument has the same effect as.

Sets the default display mode of theobject. In select mode, the cursor appears as an I-beam within thedisplay area. You can click and drag with the mouse to select a range of values. Mouse activity will causeto generate update messages, according to the mouseoutput setting.

Sets an alternative loop selection style that uses vertical mouse movement to grow and shrink the selection length, while horizontal movement is mapped to position. This works well to control aobject. When loop mode is selected, moving your cursor inside the display area changes its appearance to a double I-beam.

Sets the move display mode of theobject. This mode allows you to navigate theview. Vertical mouse movement lets you zoom in and out, while horizontal movement scrolls through the time range of the x-axis. Clicking on a point in the graph makes it the center reference point for the rest of the mouse event (until the mouse button is released). This lets you "grab" a spot and zoom in on it without having to constantly re-center the display.

Sets the draw display mode of theobject. This mode allows you to edit the values of the target, using a pencil tool. Clicking and dragging in draw mode directly changes thesamples, and can not be undone. Sample values are interpolated linearly as you drag, resulting in a continuous change, even if you are zoomed out too far to see the individual samples.

attributes.name: setunit
attributes.description: Sets the unit of time measurement used by the display.

choices.label: Sets the display unit to milliseconds (the default).

choices.digest: Set timing to sample position in the
choices.label: Causes time values to be shown as sample positions in the target. The first sample is numbered 0, unless the display has been shifted by themessage.

choices.digest: Set timing to phase within the
choices.label: Causes time to be displayed according to phase within the, normalized so that the 0 refers to the first sample, and 1 refers to the last. This type of measurement unit is especially relevant when working with objects that use 0-1 signal sync, such asand.

choices.digest: Set timing to beats per minute
choices.label: Specifies beats per minute as the time reference unit, relative to a tempo and number of beats per bar, both of which you can set with themessage.can also calculate a tempo that fits your current selection, via themessage.

attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: snapto
attributes.description: Sets the snap mode of theselection range.causes the start and end points of the selection to automatically move to specific points in the, defined by the snap mode.

choices.label: Disables snap to allow free selection (the default).

choices.digest: Snap start and end point to vertical grid lines
choices.label: Specifies that the selection start and end points should snap to the vertical grid lines, as set by theattribute. Since the spacing of the grid lines is affected by the current time measurement unit, and by the offset value (if an offset has been specified), snap to grid will be affected by these parameters as well.

attributes.name: style
attributes.description: Sets theto be applied to the object. Styles can be set using the.

attributes.name: ticks
attributes.description: Specifies the number of ticks that should be drawn between each grid line. The default is eight. An argument of, or no argument, disables the tick marks.

attributes.name: varname
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: vlabels
attributes.description: Toggles the drawing of vertical axis labels along the rightmost edge of thedisplay. Any non-zero number causes the labels to be drawn. An argument of, or no argument, disables them.

attributes.name: voffset
attributes.description: Sets the vertical offset of thedisplay. A value of 0. places the x-axis in the middle, which is the default.

attributes.name: vticks
attributes.description: Disables or enables display of the vertical axis tick marks along the left and right edges of thedisplay. Any non-zero int causes the tick marks to be drawn. An argument of, or no argument, disables them.

attributes.name: vzoom
attributes.description: Sets the vertical scaling of thedisplay.

attributes.name: waveformcolor
attributes.description: Sets the foreground color in RGBA format used to draw thedata as a waveform graph. Theattribute is mapped to thestyle color.

attributes.name: zoom_orientation
attributes.description: Change the zoom orientation depending on mouse direction.

choices.digest: Zoom when mouse is moved up
Zoom when mouse is moved down

attributes.name: zoomstyle
attributes.description: Sets drawing style when zoomed-in

choices.digest: Draw waveform as bars above or below zero

attributes.name: zoomthresh
attributes.description: If the pixel-to-sample ratio (zoom factor) is greater than or equal to, the zoomed-in drawing style is used instead of the filled-in gradient. If the value ofis 0, the zoomed-in drawing style is never used.

messages.name: (drag)
messages.digest: Function depends onattribute
messages.description: Click and drag behavior for theobject varies according to the object's mode of operation (see theattribute).

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.digest: Click and drag to manipulate the buffer contents
messages.description: The way that theobject responds to clicking and dragging varies according to how the object is configured using theattribute.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: A bang in any inlet will causeto dump/output the value to which it is set specific to the inlet in which theis received.

messages.name: bpm
messages.digest: Specify beats per minute as the time reference unit
messages.description: Specifies beats per minute as the time reference unit, relative to a tempo and number of beats per bar, both of which you can set with themessage.can also calculate a tempo that fits your current selection, via themessage.

messages.name: buftime
messages.digest: Set the minimum drawing interval in milliseconds when aobject is redrawn
messages.description: The word, followed by a number between 20 and 60000, sets the minimum drawing interval in milliseconds when aobject is redrawn due to changes in its associatedobject. Setting a higher number value will make some difference in CPU utilization. The default value is 500ms.

messages.name: crop
messages.digest: Crop thecontents to the current selection
messages.description: Themessage will trim the audio data in the targetto the current selection. It resizes theto the selection length, copies the selected samples into it, and displays the result at default settings. Theis erased, except for the selected range. This is a "destructive edit," and cannot be undone.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the display start time in milliseconds. Changing this value will offset and/or zoom the view, so that the requested time in thesample data is aligned to the left edge of the display. The default is 0 (display starts at the beginning of the target).In 2nd inlet: Sets the display length in milliseconds. The default is the length of the.In 3rd inlet: Sets the start time of the selection range in milliseconds.In 4th inlet: Sets the end time of the selection range in milliseconds.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Function depends on inlet (data converted to floats)
messages.description: Converted tospecific to each inlet.In left inlet: Sets the display start time in milliseconds. Changing this value will offset and/or zoom the view, so that the requested time in thesample data is aligned to the left edge of the display. The default is 0 (display starts at the beginning of the target).In 2nd inlet: Sets the display length in milliseconds. The default is the length of the.In 3rd inlet: Sets the start time of the selection range in milliseconds.In 4th inlet: Sets the end time of the selection range in milliseconds.

messages.name: line
messages.digest: Draw a vertical line on the display
messages.description: The word, followed by a integer or floating point value representing a time in milliseconds, will cause a vertical line to be superimposed on the waveform display at the millisecond point indicated by the argument. The purpose of this is to be able to visually indicate where the playback point of the waveform is at any given moment. If the argument ofis a negative value, the vertical line will be hidden.The word, followed by a symbol, defines the unit used to display the line. The options are:bpm: beats per minutems: milliseconds (the default)phase: phase (range 0. - 1.0)samples

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Receive link data from otherobjects
messages.description: In 5th inlet: The 5th inlet provides a link input, which allows any number ofobjects to share their start, length, select start, and select end values. Whenever any of these values changes,sends them all as a list out its right outlet. If this outlet is connected to the link input of anotherobject, it will be updated as it receives the lists.To complete the circuit, the secondobject's list output can be connected to the link input of the first. Then, changes in either one (via mouse clicks, etc.) will be reflected in the other. This is mainly useful when theobjects are viewing different channels of the same. Any number ofobjects can be linked in this fashion, forming one long, circular chain of links. In this casewill prevent feedback from occurring.
messages.argPattern: start:float, length:float, select-start:float, select-end:float, select-start-ms:int, select-end-ms:int

messages.name: mode
messages.digest: Set legacy mouse response mode
messages.description: This is a legacy message - this functionality is now provided by theattribute.

messages.name: mouseoutput
messages.digest: Determine when start and end mouse output is sent
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol argument, determines when selection start and end values are sent in response to mouse activity. Only the selection start and end (outlets 3 and 4) are affected. Mouse information is always sent from outlet 5, regardless of the mouseoutput mode. Valid symbol arguments are,,,,, and.- Selection start and end values are not sent in response to mouse activity. Sending themessage with no argument has the same effect as the same message with the argument.- Causes the current selection start and end values to be sent (from outlets 3 and 4) only when you click inside the.- Causes selection start and end to be sent only when you release the mouse button, after clicking inside the.- Causes selection start and end to be sent both when you click inside the, and when the mouse button is released.- Causes selection start and end to be sent on click, release, and throughout the drag operation, whenever the values change.

messages.name: name
messages.digest: Linkto a namedobject and display contents
messages.description: Identical to themessage. The word, followed by a symbol which is the name of aobject, linksto the target, which is drawn with default display values. An optional int argument sets the channel offset, for viewing multi-channelobjects. The name of the linkedis copied to theattribute and the channel offset is copied to theattribute. Both are saved with the patcher.If themessage is sent with no arguments, it will clear the.

messages.name: normalize
messages.digest: Normalize thecontents
messages.description: The word, followed by a float, will scale the sample values in the targetso that the highest peak matches the value given by the argument. This can cause either amplification or attenuation of the audio, but in either case, everyvalue is scaled, and this activity cannot be undone.

messages.name: replacebuffercontents
messages.digest: Replacecontents and display new contents
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol argument, will replace the current contents of the buffer with which theobject is associated and display the new buffer contents.

messages.name: set
messages.digest: Linkto a namedobject and display contents
messages.description: Identical to themessage. The word, followed by a symbol which is the name of aobject, linksto the target, which is drawn with default display values. An optional int argument sets the channel offset, for viewing multi-channelobjects. The name of the linkedis copied to theattribute and the channel offset is copied to theattribute. Both are saved with the patcher.If themessage is sent with no arguments, it will clear the.

messages.name: setbpm
messages.digest: Calculate a new tempo based on the current selection range
messages.description: The word, with no arguments, causesto calculate a tempo based on the current selection range. It automatically changes the display time unit to bpm, as if you had sent the message. A tempo is selected such that the selection range constitutes a logical multiple or subdivision of the bar, preserving the current beats per bar value, and attempting to find the closest value to the current tempo that satisfies its criteria. When a suitable tempo is selected, the offset parameter is adjusted so that the start time of the selection range falls exactly on a bar line.The result is that the selection area will be framed precisely by a compatible tempo. One use of this technique is to quickly establish time labels and tick marks for a section of audio. After selecting a bar as accurately as possible, sending themessage and turning on snap to label allows immediate quantization of the selection range to metric values.If the targetcontains an audio segment that is already cropped to a logical number of beats or bars, the best technique is to select the entire range of the(with messages to the select start and end inlets), followed by themessage. If theis cropped precisely, the resulting tempo overlay should be quite accurate, and immediately reveal the tempo along with metric information.When a new tempo is calculated, it is sent from the rightmost outlet (the link outlet), to update any linkedobjects, and to be used in whatever manner required by the surrounding patch.

messages.name: snap
messages.digest: Sets the snap mode of the selection range
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol argument, Sets the snap mode of theselection range.causes the start and end points of the selection to automatically move to specific points in the, defined by the snap mode. Possible arguments are,, and.- Disables snap to allow free selection. This is the default. Themessage with no argument has the same effect.- Specifies that the selection start and end points should snap to the vertical grid lines, as set by themessage. Since the spacing of the grid lines is affected by the current time measurement unit, and by the offset value (if an offset has been specified), snap to grid will be affected by these parameters as well.- Causes the selection start and end to snap to the tick divisions specified by the ticks message.- Instead of snapping the selection to a uniform grid, this mode searches for zero-crossings of thedata. These are defined as the points where a positive sample follows a negative sample, or vice-versa. This can be useful to find loop and edit points.

messages.name: undo
messages.digest: Revert waveform selection to previous start and end points
messages.description: This mode works forselection only. It causes the selection start and end points to revert to their immediately previous values. This is helpful when you are making fine editing adjustments with the mouse and accidentally click in the wrong place, or otherwise cause the selection to change unintentionally. Repeatedcommands will toggle between the last two selection states.

messages.name: unit
messages.digest: Set the unit of time measurement used by the display
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol argument, sets the unit of time measurement used by the display. Valid symbol arguments are,,, and.- Sets the display unit to milliseconds. This is the default.- Causes time values to be shown as sample positions in the target. The first sample is numbered 0, unless the display has been shifted by themessage.- Causes time to be displayed according to phase within the, normalized so that the 0 refers to the first sample, and 1 refers to the last. This type of measurement unit is especially relevant when working with objects that use 0-1 signal sync, such asand.- Specifies beats per minute as the time reference unit, relative to a tempo and number of beats per bar, both of which you can set with themessage.can also calculate a tempo that fits your current selection, via themessage.
